source_summary: Ink-and-light-wash Chinese landscape with misty distant hills, clustered rocky mountains, layered slopes, groves of leafed and bare trees, and a small waterside pavilion at the lower right. Calligraphy, seals, borders, and paper texture are excluded from motifs.

motifs.name: left_misty_peak
motifs.description: Isolate the soft triangular distant hill on the left-middle with pale ink washes, blurred ridge edges, and the surrounding light misty valley forms below and to its right; exclude nearby red seals and inscriptions.
must_preserve: soft graded ink wash on the hill mass
irregular dry-brush ridge contour
small horizontal pale gaps suggesting mist or terraces
faint valley washes fading into blank space

motifs.name: central_mist_water_passage
motifs.description: Isolate the pale horizontal opening between the left hill and central rocks, reading as mist or water receding into the landscape, with faint banks and soft broken washes.
must_preserve: unpainted negative space forming the mist channel
faint grey washes along both banks
broken horizontal strokes suggesting water or haze
soft feathered edges where hills dissolve into mist

motifs.name: central_rocky_cliff_pines
motifs.description: Isolate the central vertical rocky cliff group with stacked ledges and dark pine-like foliage clinging to the left and top edges, excluding the red seal above and unrelated foreground trees below.
must_preserve: vertical dry-brush rock texture
dark horizontal pine clusters on ledges
layered ink washes defining cliff faces
broken contour lines and pale interior highlights

motifs.name: upper_right_main_mountain
motifs.description: Isolate the large upper-right mountain peak and adjoining distant ridge, with dark crown foliage, pale diagonal ravines, mist bands, and soft receding hills; exclude the nearby circular red seal.
must_preserve: dark stippled brushwork across the summit
pale diagonal ravine washes
soft cloud-like mist bands crossing the slopes
faded distant ridge on the far right
granular ink texture along the mountain contour

motifs.name: mid_right_layered_hillside
motifs.description: Isolate the middle-right sloping hillside beneath the main mountain, including layered terraces, scattered dark shrub marks, and the pale sweeping bank descending toward the right.
must_preserve: long curved terrace lines
light grey wash planes between ledges
dark clustered shrub dots and short strokes
softly broken ridge edges
subtle color warmth in the pale earth wash

motifs.name: left_foreground_willow_grove
motifs.description: Isolate the left foreground grove of thin leaning trunks and bare branch sprays mixed with dark leafy clumps, including the low rocks at their base; avoid the large red seal to the left.
must_preserve: slender calligraphic trunk lines
forking bare branches
dark leaf clusters made of short wet strokes
pale ochre-grey trunk accents
rounded foreground rock washes

motifs.name: central_foreground_grove_rocks
motifs.description: Isolate the dense central foreground thicket with multiple pale trunks, dark foliage masses, and interlocking rocks and ground washes across the base.
must_preserve: overlapping pale tree trunks with dark outlines
irregular black-green foliage clusters
dry-brush texture on roots and rocks
low horizontal ground washes
branch tips extending upward into open mist

motifs.name: lower_right_waterside_pavilion
motifs.description: Isolate the small pavilion at the lower right beside water, together with its adjacent trees, sloped bank, and reflected/stepped structural lines below the roof.
must_preserve: simple angular roof geometry
thin vertical support posts
dark tree canopies framing the pavilion
sloping shoreline wash
delicate linear marks suggesting reflection or railing
pale open water around the structure

planning_prompt:
Analyze this Chinese landscape painting as a source for a motif bank.

Create exactly 8 reusable motifs. Return JSON only.

For each motif:
- Use a short snake_case name.
- Describe what should be isolated.
- Provide a normalized bbox as [x, y, width, height], where 0,0 is the top-left of the full image.
- Include all visible brushwork for that motif, but do not include unrelated neighboring motifs.
- Prefer motifs that can be recombined into a new coherent Chinese painting: mountains, hillsides, village clusters, pavilion groups, water/lotus surfaces, bridges, scholar figures, boats, clouds, rocks, shrubs, pines, willows, bamboo.
- Capture details that must be preserved: linework, wash texture, roof geometry, tree needles, rock texture, mist edges, and color accents.

Do not invent objects that are not visible in the source image.
Do not include calligraphy, seals, labels, borders, or paper texture as motifs unless explicitly requested.
